name: Balaam
overview: Balaam is a male figure from Pethor in Mesopotamia, as identified in Numbers 22:5 and Deuteronomy 23:4. The biblical text does not specify his tribal affiliation or additional personal notes beyond his origin. His background places him geographically outside the Israelite community.
namesAndTitles: The name Balaam may mean 'Baal of the people,' 'the clan brings forth,' or 'devourer, glutton,' reflecting possible Hebrew roots. This proper name, given not by God, suggests a complex cultural or linguistic background connected to the ancient Near Eastern milieu.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Balaam as the son of Beor, according to Numbers 22:5. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Balaam's significance in Scripture stems from his role as a non-Israelite prophet from Mesopotamia, whose interactions with Israel highlight God's sovereignty over all nations. His origin and lineage emphasize his position as an outsider called into the biblical narrative, underscoring God's control over those beyond Israel's borders. Balaam's story serves as a reminder of God's authority and the challenges posed by foreign influences.
